# HE Labs: Where Innovation Becomes Operational Advantage

HE Labs™ is Hotel Equities' dedicated innovation and incubation division, a structured platform for evaluating technologies, developing AI-enabled workflows, incubating hospitality concepts, and scaling what works. Hospitality does not lack new ideas or technologies. What it has lacked is a disciplined way to turn them into a scalable operating advantage.

# Why HE Labs Matters Now

The hospitality industry in its current state is becoming harder to sustain. Costs have increased faster than revenues, and the balance of profit between brands, operators, and owners has increasingly tilted toward the “asset light” players in the industry.

At the same time, hospitality has struggled to consistently turn innovation into a scalable operational advantage. The industry needs smarter systems that improve efficiency, enhance the guest experience, and better connect innovation with day-to-day hotel operations, all while remaining rooted in a people-first business. HE Labs was created to help bridge that gap.

# Built to Maximize Owner Returns

Hotel management companies are built to operate assets, not to evaluate technologies or systematically scale innovation. HE Labs exists to fill that gap, providing a structured approach to evaluating, testing, and scaling innovation.

From revenue optimization tools to operational efficiencies and enhanced guest experiences, initiatives are designed to deliver stronger, more consistent returns for owners.

# Key Owner Benefits

### Structured Evaluation

Technology and workflows are assessed against defined problems, operating context, and measurable success criteria.

### Real-World Testing

Initiatives are validated in live operating environments before broader implementation.

### Operational Alignment

Innovation is built to work within operations, reducing friction and supporting smoother implementation.

### Scalable Results

Proven solutions move forward, creating long-term value across the portfolio.

# How it Works

HE Labs applies a disciplined approach to innovation through opportunity selection, system design, real-world testing, and scaling what works.

## Evaluate the Opportunity

Every initiative begins with a clearly defined problem, opportunity, and success criteria. 

## Design the Right System

Technology and workflow decisions are approached as part of a broader operating system—not as isolated tools. 

## Test in Real Environments

Pilots run in live environments, ensuring results reflect real operational conditions. 

## Scale What Works

Only validated solutions move forward into broader implementation.

Hotel Equities Appoints Brian Jenkins to Lead HE Labs, the Management Company’s New Innovation Division 

### Hotel Equities Appoints Brian Jenkins to Lead HE Labs, the Management Company’s New Innovation Division 

 May 29, 2026 

ATLANTA, Ga. — Hotel Equities (HE), a best-in-class hospitality operator, announces the appointment of Brian Jenkins as Head of HE Labs™, Hotel Equities' dedicated innovation and incubation platform built for evaluating emerging technologies, developing AI-driven workflows, and advancing new operating models designed to improve owner returns and hotel performance across the portfolio. In this role, Jenkins will oversee all HE Labs initiatives, from testing and evaluation to deployment, ensuring each advances through a defined progression before being implemented at the property-level and scaled.

"Brian's background sits at the intersection of strategy and hospitality operations, and that combination is precisely what this role demands,” said Ben Rafter, Chief Executive Officer of Hotel Equities. “The industry has never had a shortage of technologies; what it has lacked is the discipline to evaluate them rigorously, integrate them seamlessly, and deploy only those that move the needle. HE Labs exists to deliver validated solutions to owners, not experiments, and Brian brings the discipline, operating perspective, and analytical rigor required to lead that work."

"The gap between what technology promises and what it actually delivers for owners is where HE Labs operates,” said Jenkins. “This is the right moment for this kind of platform. Our focus is to bring discipline to that gap: evaluating what works, deploying what fits, and scaling solutions that improve performance.”

Before leading HE Labs, Jenkins served as Executive Vice President of Strategic Initiatives, shaping Hotel Equities' broader technology and innovation strategy, conducting business development, and applying quantitative analysis to operational decision-making, including the development of the Hospitality Intelligence (H.I.) platform, Springboard's proprietary system blending technology and human insight to enhance operational efficiency. Previously, Jenkins held a series of strategic roles at Springboard Hospitality, which he joined in 2016 ahead of its combination with Hotel Equities in 2025. 

Before entering hospitality, Jenkins was a strategy consultant at Capco in New York, where he advised leading financial institutions on IT strategy, organizational restructuring, change management, and risk management. He holds a B.A. in Financial Economics from Columbia University.

For more information about Hotel Equities and its leadership, visit www.hotelequities.com/meet-our-team.htm. To learn more about HE Labs™, visit www.hotelequities.com/he-labs.htm.

Get to know the dedicated professionals who drive our culture, performance, and commitment to delivering excellence in hospitality. # Executive Team

Benjamin Rafter

Chief Executive Officer 

Benjamin Rafter

Chief Executive Officer

Ben Rafter is the Chief Executive Officer of Hotel Equities, a leading hospitality management and development firm with a portfolio of hotels, resorts, and outdoor hospitality destinations spanning the United States, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. A recognized innovator at the intersection of hospitality and technology, Rafter assumed leadership of the combined Hotel Equities and Springboard Hospitality organization in May 2025, bringing with him a track record of building tech-forward operating platforms, including Hospitality Intelligence (H.I.) and HE Labs, that drive measurable performance for owners. Earlier in his career, he led Aqua Hospitality to become the largest hotel operator in Hawaii and co-founded Innerlinx (LiveBid), which was acquired by Amazon.com. Hotel Equities is formalising its technology strategy to improve profit margins, focusing on automation and AI solutions as sector economics come under strain from inflation and labour costs.

For years, hotel companies have promised owners that strong room rates would eventually translate into healthier profits. That argument has worn thin. Ben Rafter, chief executive of Hotel Equities, told Skift that the economics of the sector are under strain, arguing that branded groups may be performing acceptably while property owners remain squeezed by inflation, labour costs and other expenses.

How this was made

Read, scored and filed before anyone asked a question.

Noah reads about 1.96 million news events a week, front pages included, and scores every one for direction and analytical markers against a standing index. This piece was written against that evidence base.

Hotel Equities is now trying to respond by formalising its technology strategy through HE Labs, a new internal effort designed to identify tools that can improve margins and help employees adopt them more quickly. According to the company, the priority is not novelty for its own sake but practical systems that reduce costs and make operations run more efficiently.

Brian Jenkins, a former management and technology consultant who is leading the initiative, has focused the early work on areas such as automating back-office accounting and using AI to improve labour scheduling. The company is also looking at robotics, although early experiments in hotel operations have not always delivered the gains operators hoped for.

The push comes as Hotel Equities has been reshaped by its merger with Springboard Hospitality, a deal that created a manager overseeing more than 250 hotels across branded, independent and lifestyle properties. Rafter became chief executive of the combined business, which has also been broadening its leadership team. Against that backdrop, Wall Street is starting to view AI as a more credible profit tool for hotels, with J.P. Morgan recently suggesting 2026 could be the first year such investments start to pay off in earnings terms.
